subject: Renewal: Brightline capacity planning — staged commit & credit options
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@brightline.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — Q3 surge and options

Hi Ethan,

Hope youre well. Were starting renewal planning for our account and Q3 looks like it will be a big usage quarter for Brightline (marketing push + two acquisitions). Our finance team is asking for predictable unit pricing and some protection against mid-year demand spikes.

High level asks from our side:
- A price hold for committed units for at least 6 months (ideally 9).
- A staged commit option so we can ramp cleanly (we can commit to a lower Qty in year 1 and scale up).
- A burst/buffer pool for spikes with credits for sustained overage vs punitive overage rates.

Ive attached our Q3 usage report so you can see where the risk is concentrated. Can you propose 2-3 paths (conservative commit, ramp plan, and an aggressive commit with deeper discount) and any onboarding/true-up credit options? Procurement will need an outline to review. Im looping Rohit (ops) and procurement when we get a firmer plan.

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Head of Platform — Brightline Media
attachments: Brightline_Q3_usage_report.pdf

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q3 surge and options

Anika,

Thanks for the usage report and the clear ask. I pulled a quick draft with three paths (conservative, staged ramp, and committed accelerator). High-level summary below; attached is a short proposal PDF with bullets and ballpark economics.

1) Conservative commit (low risk):
   - Year 1 commit = 60% of current annualized usage
   - No price hold beyond 3 months
   - Burst pool available at standard overage rate + 25% credit applied for sustained monthly overage >20%

2) Staged ramp (recommended):
   - Year 1 commit = 70%
   - Year 2 commit = ramp to 110% (true-up at each billing cycle)
   - Price hold: 9 months on committed unit price
   - Credits: $/token onboarding credit up to $50k applied against overage in Q1

3) Aggressive commit (discounted):
   - Multi-year commit (2 yrs) with up-front discount: 12% off committed unit price
   - Stronger burst allowance (larger pool) with 50% reduced overage multiplier for first 6 months

Operational asks from Redwood:
- A mid-year review clause to rebaseline commits if usage materially deviates (we can do this quarterly).
- DocuSign for the addendum and an itemized invoice schedule.

Im ccing Monica from CS to confirm onboarding credits and Ben for quick pricing approval if we need to extend beyond standard concessions. Please let me know which path you want us to formalize; if its helpful I can push a detailed XLS with month-by-month true-up and invoice timing.

Regards,
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf

Also please include a DocuSign link when you send the formal addendum.

Thanks,
Anika

Anika / procurement team,

Thanks 11 happy to confirm the staged ramp can include a 9-month price hold as requested. Below is the more formalized path we recommend (we can turn this into a redline-ready addendum once you confirm):

Staged Ramp Proposal (recommended):
- Year 1 committed units: 70% of current annualized usage (monthly true-up)
- Year 2 committed units: planned ramp to 110% with a scheduled true-up at each billing cycle
- Committed unit price: locked for 9 months from effective date
- Burst pool: 15% of monthly committed capacity reserved as shared burst (billed monthly when used)
- Overage treatment: sustained monthly overage >20% triggers a credit schedule: 25% credit on overage effective month 2; sustained >40% triggers optional temporary burst increase (capacity on loan)
- Onboarding credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice for migration and integration support
- Invoice cadence: We can support a 60/40 split across quarters; I'll include an invoice schedule in the addendum

Im attaching an XLS with a month-by-month example and the invoice split (file: Redwood_Staged_Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx). If this looks good I will:
1) Generate the addendum and DocuSign link
2) Loop in finance to finalize invoice wording and payment terms
3) Confirm any operational SLAs for the burst pool with Monica

Quote: This structure is contingent on a signed addendum by 2026-07-15 to lock the 9-month price hold and onboarding credit.
